panels.description: Request success rate. Normal (green) if 99.5% or above, risky (red) if below 98%. Only counts successful completions where finished_reason='stop'.
panels.title: Success Rate

panels.description: Number of currently processing (Running) + waiting (Waiting) requests. A sudden increase is a sign of a traffic spike.
panels.title: Active Requests

panels.description: Scheduler efficiency. Running/(Running+Waiting). 100% means all requests are processed immediately. Below 70% indicates overload.
panels.title: System Efficiency

panels.description: Time taken until the first token is generated (P99). Key metric for perceived user response speed. Ideally under 1 second.
panels.title: TTFT P99

panels.description: [Critical] Preemption rate. Occurs when running requests are interrupted due to insufficient KV Cache. If > 0, immediate investigation is required. Consider increasing GPU memory or decreasing batch size.
panels.title: Preemption Rate

panels.description: Total time from request receipt to response completion. P50 is the median, P99 is the 99th percentile. Spikes in P99 indicate bottlenecks.
panels.title: E2E Request Latency

panels.description: Ratio of Prefill (input processing) vs Decode (output generation) latency. High prefill indicates long input prompts; high decode indicates long output generation.
panels.title: Inference Stage Breakdown

panels.description: Comparison of TTFT (Time to First Token) vs TPOT (Time Per Output Token). High TTFT suggests prefill bottleneck; high TPOT suggests decode bottleneck.
panels.title: TTFT vs TPOT

panels.description: Tokens processed per second. Input(Prompt) = input tokens, Output(Generation) = output tokens. Higher throughput indicates better system efficiency.
panels.title: Token Throughput

panels.description: Ratio of output tokens to input tokens. High ratio = long input + short output (RAG); low ratio = short input + long output (generation/summarization).
panels.title: Token I/O Ratio

panels.description: Percentage of computations saved by Prefix Cache. Higher means more prefill operations are skipped via cache, saving GPU resources. (1 - actual_computed / total_input) * 100
panels.title: Prefix Cache Savings

panels.description: Distribution of input token counts per request. Darker colors indicate more requests of that length. Concentration in certain ranges may require length-based optimization.
panels.title: Request Length Heatmap (Prompt)

panels.description: Time requests spend waiting in the queue. Increases if the GPU is busy. Persistent high values suggest a need for instance scaling.
panels.title: Request Queue Time

panels.description: GPU KV Cache usage. Memory area used to store intermediate computation results. Above 80% is caution; above 95% risks Preemption.
panels.title: GPU KV Cache Usage

panels.description: Prefix Cache hit rate. Percentage of requests reusing system prompts or few-shot examples. >70% is efficient; key metric for RAG environments.
panels.title: Prefix Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Number of requests by scheduler state. Running=inferring on GPU, Waiting=in queue, Swapped=memory swapped. Persistent increase in Waiting indicates overload.
panels.title: Scheduler State

panels.description: Python GC event frequency and process memory usage. Frequent GC or steadily increasing RSS may indicate a memory leak.
panels.title: Python GC & Memory

panels.description: Distribution of request completion reasons. stop=normal completion (EOS), length=max length reached, abort=interrupted. High abort rate is problematic.
panels.title: Finish Reason Distribution

panels.description: Trend of total throughput vs successful requests. A gap indicates failed requests. They should consistently match for normal operation.
panels.title: Throughput vs Success
Routing Split
panels.description: Total number of requests split by classification. Shows the distribution between DIRECT and REASONING modes.

panels.title: Request Rate by Mode
panels.description: Rate of requests per second categorized by classification (DIRECT or REASONING).

panels.title: Classify Latency
panels.description: Latency of the classification process, shown in percentiles (p50, p95, p99).
